The '''chemical industry of India''' is a major industry in the [[Economy of India|Indian economy]] and as of 2022, contributes 7% of the country's Gross Domestic Product ([[Gross domestic product|GDP]]).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Awasthi |first=Anurag |date=6 September 2022 |title=In the global semiconductor race, India's chip manufacturing needs to get the 'chemistry' right |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/sme-sector/in-the-global-semiconductor-race-indias-chip-manufacturing-needs-to-get-the-chemistry-right/articleshow/93996080.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-01-06}}</ref> India is the world's sixth largest producer of chemicals and the third largest in [[Asia]], as of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 April 2022 |title=Exports of Indian chemicals register growth of 106% in 2021-22 over 2013-14 |url=https://pib.gov.in/pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1820478 |access-date=2023-01-06 |website=pib.gov.in}}</ref> The value of the Indian chemical industry was estimated at $100 billion dollars in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Topic: Chemical industry in India|url=https://www.statista.com/topics/5601/chemical-industry-in-india/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200526083156/https://www.statista.com/topics/5601/chemical-industry-in-india/ |archive-date=26 May 2020 |access-date=2020-09-02|website=Statista|language=en}}</ref> The chemical industry of India generates employment for five million people.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sectors|url=https://www.cii.in/sectors.aspx?enc=prvePUj2bdMtgTmvPwvisYH+5EnGjyGXO9hLECvTuNskmvgGjRIRgzWycLq2dn10|access-date=2020-09-02|website=www.cii.in}}</ref> The Indian chemical industry produces 80,000 different chemical products. India was also the third largest producer of plastic in 2019. As of September 2019, the [[Alkaline earth metal|alkali chemical]] industry produced 71% of all chemicals produced in India.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chemical Industry in India – Indian Chemical Sector Analysis|url=https://www.investindia.gov.in/sector/chemicals|access-date=2020-09-02|website=www.investindia.gov.in|language=en}}</ref> India's chemical industry accounts about 14% of production in Indian industries.<ref>{{Cite web|last=PricewaterhouseCoopers|title=Chemicals|url=https://www.pwc.in/industries/chemicals.html|access-date=2020-09-07|website=PwC|language=en-in}}</ref>

==Introduction==
The Indian chemical industry mainly produces basic types of chemicals as well as knowledge type chemicals and specialty type chemicals as of 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=India - chemical market share by type 2018|url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/1062458/india-chemical-market-share-by-type/|access-date=2020-09-03|website=Statista|language=en}}</ref>  In India, [[Gujarat]] was the largest state contributor to the chemical industry of India in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=India - chemical industry share by state 2018|url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/1062442/india-chemical-industry-share-by-state/|access-date=2020-09-03|website=Statista|language=en}}</ref>  India also produces products related to [[petrochemical]]s, [[Fertilizer|fertilizers]], [[paint]]s, [[varnish]]es, [[glass]], [[perfume]]s, [[toiletries]], [[pharmaceuticals]], etc.

== Production ==
The chemicals industry in India is very diversified and can essentially be classified into 6 categories: bulk chemicals, specialty chemicals, agrochemicals, petrochemicals, polymers and fertilisers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2022 |title=Chemical Industry, Chemicals Manufacturers and Exporters in India - IBEF |url=https://www.ibef.org/industry/chemical-industry-india |access-date=2022-06-13 |website=India Brand Equity Foundation |language=en}}</ref>

===Basic organic chemicals===
The organic chemicals industry is one of the most significant sectors of the chemical industry in the world. It plays a vital role in providing inputs for other industries of [[paint]]s, [[adhesive]]s, [[Pharmaceutical industry in India|pharmaceuticals]], [[dyestuff]]s and [[Intermediate 1|intermediates]], leather chemicals, [[pesticide]]s, etc. [[Methanol]], [[acetic acid]], [[formaldehyde]], [[pyridine]], [[phenol]], [[Aliphatic amine|alkylamines]], [[ethyl acetate]], and [[acetic anhydride]] are major basic organic chemicals that are produced in India. Six major chemicals are produced in India: [[methanol]], [[aniline]], [[Aliphatic amine|alkylamines]], and its derivatives [[formaldehyde]], [[acetic acid]], and [[phenol]] contributing to nearly 2/3 of Indian basic organic chemical industry. The country has several basic organic chemical companies that are among the largest companies globally in their chemical productions. These companies include:

* Balaji Amines. The worlds largest producer of [[Dimethylamine|Dimethylamine hydrochloride]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Karim |first=Abdul |date=30 December 2019 |title=Pick of the week: Balaji Amines Ltd |url=https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.research.pdf/Balaji%20Amines%20-%20Pick%20of%20the%20Week%20-%20301219-min.pdf |access-date=15 May 2022 |website=HDFC Securities |page=3}}</ref>

=== Inorganic chemicals ===

==== Chlor-alkali chemicals ====
In India, [[Chloralkali process|chlor-alkali]] the sector mainly consists of the production of three [[inorganic chemicals]]; [[caustic soda]] ({{chem|Na|O|H)}}, [[chlorine]] ({{chem|Cl|2}}) and [[soda ash]] ({{chem|Na|2|C|O|3}}).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.omrglobal.com/industry-reports/india-chlor-alkali-market|title=Indian Chlor Alkali Market Size, Share, Trends and Industry Analysis|website=Orion Market Research}}</ref>  Hydrogen is also produced in this industry in small amounts. The chlor-alkali industry inputs are mainly used in soaps and [[detergents]], [[Pulp (paper)|pulp]] and [[paper]], [[textiles]], [[aluminium]] processing industry for [[caustic soda]] and for [[soda ash]] in [[glass]], [[silicate]] production etc apart from [[Soap|soaps]] and [[detergents]].
In the financial year 2019–2020 of chlor-alkali industry of India over four million metric tons of alkali chemicals were produced. The products that are produced in this industry are [[soda ash]], [[caustic soda]], and liquid [[chlorine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/726866/india-alkali-chemicals-production-volume/|title=India - alkali chemicals production volume 2020|website=Statista}}</text></ref> [[Tata Chemicals]], a diversified Indian chemicals company, is also the world's third largest manufacturer of soda ash.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yadavalli |first=Sai Prabhakar |date=19 February 2022 |title=Why you should accumulate Tata Chemicals stock |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/portfolio/stock-fundamental-analysis-india/why-you-should-accumulate-tata-chemicals-stock/article65063102.ece |access-date=18 May 2022 |website=Business Line}}</ref>

=== Speciality chemicals ===
As of December 2021, the [[speciality chemicals]] segment comprised 22% of India's overall chemicals market.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Gaurav |date=20 December 2021 |title=India's chemical industry will continue on growth path, says JM Financial |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/indias-chemical-industry-will-continue-on-growth-path-says-jm-financial-7841371.html |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en}}</ref> In 2019, India's share of the global speciality chemicals market stood at 4%, however India's market share is projected to stand at 5.5% by 2025.<ref name=":0" /> India has several niche specialty chemical companies that are among the largest companies globally in their specific niche sectors. These companies include: 

* [[Camlin Fine Sciences]]. The world's third largest manufacturer of [[vanillin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Green |first=Elizabeth |date=12 July 2017 |title=Camlin Fine Sciences Becomes World's Third-Largest Vanillin Producer |url=https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/camlin-fine-sciences-becomes-worlds-third-largest-vanillin-producer.html |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=.foodingredientsfirst.com/ |language=en}}</ref>
* Clean Science and Technology. The world's third largest producer of [[guaiacol]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Shah |first1=Mitesh |last2=Shah |first2=Dhavan |last3=Khandekar |first3=Siddhant |date=6 July 2021 |title=Clean Science and Technology Ltd |url=https://www.icicidirect.com/mailimages/IDirect_CleanScience_IPOReview.pdf |access-date=10 May 2022 |website=ICICI Direct |page=4 }}</ref>
* Tatva Chintan. The world's second largest manufacturer of structure directing agents for [[Zeolite|zeolites]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Shah |first1=Mitesh |last2=Shah |first2=Dhavan |last3=Khandekar |first3=Siddhant |date=15 July 2021 |title=Tatva Chintan Pharma Chem Ltd |url=https://www.icicidirect.com/mailimages/IDirect_TatvaChintanPharma_IPOReview.pdf |access-date=11 May 2022 |website=ICICI Direct |page=7 }}</ref>
